newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures rise in line with JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures rise in line with JGB gains.

text.p: Key September Euroyen futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session higher in line with gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, traders said.
September settled at an intraday high of 99.25. Volume was 43,172 contracts.
"Euroyen futures followed JGB futures higher. Tokyo stocks' sharp fall also helped to support prices," a city bank trader said.
A sizeable amount of bids was seen at 99.23 for September Euroyen, a trader at a long-term credit bank said.
Key March JGB futures ended up 0.38 at 124.11. Meanwhile, Tokyo's key Nikkei 225 stock average closed down 549.81 points or 2.83 percent at 18,896.19.
The weakness in Tokyo stocks has mixed implications for Euroyen futures, traders said.

While the Nikkei's plunge would help dash the possibility of any near-term credit tightening, Euroyen futures could be dragged down if the key stock index's plunge prompt investors to sell JGBs to cover the losses, they said.
"If the Nikkei falls further, September might test 99.30. However, the upside may be limited at around that level. It would depend on JGBs," the city bank trader said.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.49 percent, up from 0.48 percent on Monday.
The BOJ drained a net 400 billion yen from the money market in the morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 280 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent, up from 0.52 percent on Monday.
About 120 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.51 percent, unchanged from the previous session.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.50 percent, also flat from Monday.
